newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 11.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Analysts say current election campaign is dirtiest contest in 20 years. A spate of killings and blatant electoral law violations have made the November 17 vote the "dirtiest" since 1975 and 1976 elections, analysts from Nakhon Ratchasima's Rajabhat Institute say. (BANGKOK POST)

- Some 4,000 border patrol policemen have been deployed across the country to work with PollWatch to prevent violations of the election law, the deputy spokesman of the police department said. (BANGKOK POST)

- Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa claims vote buying by opposition Democrat Party is worse in parts of Bangkok, a Democrat stronghold, than in other parts of the country. Other party leaders also accused the Democrats, who claim to be running a clean campaign, of buying votes. (THE NATION)

- Stock Exchange of Thailand seen as a long-term pick in Asia. Despite the immediate problems posed by political uncertainty and the property slump threatening the asset quality of banks and finance firms, the Thai bourse is expected to outperform most regional markets in 12 months, the managing director from Crosby Securities said. (THE NATION)

- U.S. decision to lift embargo on shrimps seen brightening prospects for the Thai shrimp industry. The United States lifted the embargo after Thailand convinced Washington it has met requirements for turtle protection devices during shrimp harvesting (BANGKOK POST)

- New airport work faces delays. Thailand's Transport and Communications Minister has ordered a delay in bids for the Nong Ngu Hao airport reclamation and consturciton project after constructios firms complained of irregularities in the bidding process, ministry sources said. (BANGKOK POST)
